## Hilbert Spaces

Recall that an [[inner-product-space]] is a vector space with an inner product,
which induces a norm and hence a metric (see [[normed-space]]).

:::{.definition data-title="Hilbert Space"}

A **Hilbert space** is a **complete** inner product space, meaning that every
[[cauchy-sequence]] in the space converges to a limit within the space.

:::

Standard examples are $\mathbb{R}^n$ with the dot product, the sequence space
$\ell^2$, and $L^2(\mu)$ for a measure space $(X,\mathcal{M},\mu)$.
